body:
# the contributor audit: weighted centroid tails and subset-pair transfer


three-fiber corollary.** This audits the continuous inequality and its
stated applications, not the unrestricted OC theorem.

I independently read
`candidate dafd411c026c302c` and ran
`supporting computation verify_weighted_three_centroid_tails.py`, which passed. The proof has
the following complete, noncircular chain.

* The original centered marginal is nonatomic and 1/d-concave. A strict
  violation persists after moving ONLY the central CDF threshold a small
  amount to the negative side. The resulting affine closed-set objective
  is upper semicontinuous on a fixed compact support. Every Dirac allowed
  by the nonnegative-mean constraint has objective at most one, including
  the Dirac at zero. Thus the cited, previously audited one-constraint
  Fradelizi--Guedon theorem legitimately reduces a violation to a centered
  affine-power density. This is different from applying localization
  directly at the central atom, which would fail.

* The increasing affine-power orientation uses the already independently
  proved PAIRED-tail theorem. At the supporting-endpoint shift it gives
  exactly T_r<=1-2Gamma. Jensen for the concave quantile gives p<=1/2.
  The derivative signs before and after the supporting threshold then
  yield Gamma+1/2 for all shifts. No unproved T_3<=1/8 estimate is used;
  that stronger estimate is false and was rejected before this proof.

* For the reflected orientation, all support transitions are present.
  On the first interval the derivative changes from negative to positive
  at the stated critical point. On the next interval it decreases to the
  final value 1/2. Therefore the only possible global minima are the
  interior critical value and that final constant. The critical formula
  and its validity interval m<=(1+k)/2 are exact.

* The powered truncated mean g(R) is concave. Its displayed second
  derivative is (1-alpha) I^(1/alpha-2)(A^2-I B), whose sign is precisely
  Cauchy--Schwarz. Differentiation is only needed for R>0; continuous
  extension handles the possibly singular endpoint. The required
  numerator H is concave and both endpoints of its complete critical
  interval are nonnegative. This proves the full interval inequality,
  not just a cone or numerical endpoint case.

* The dimensional product bound is correct: d=2 is 16/27; for d>=3,
  power-mean monotonicity gives A_d>15/11 and the exact exponential-series
  bound gives Gamma>11/30. Their product is greater than 1/2. Bernoulli
  gives the strict inequality placing the critical endpoint inside the
  mean range. The d=1 and constant-density cases are handled separately.

* The measurable-subset estimate minimizes an explicitly piecewise linear
  lower bound over a in [0,V]. Its minimum is exactly at a=V-F(t).
  For t<=0 the new weighted theorem applies; for t>=0 the existing
  paired-tail theorem plus monotonicity gives the required bound. It
  follows that the actual three cap contributions are at least
  Gamma V+a/2. No density, centroid, or convexity condition is imposed on
  the measurable subset beyond its inclusion in K.

* For actual convex fibers A,K,K, the midpoint inclusion is automatic,
  the chosen point is the middle fiber's ordinary centroid, and every
  oblique cap has exactly the required three thresholds. The separately
  checked vertical closed caps contain their whole boundary fiber.
  A base-linear continuous shear treats translates of the two large
  fibers and preserves both the lattice and the fiber measure. The
  support-function argument placing the transformed A inside K is valid.

This note does not audit any sections appended after the read of
Sections 1--6; those require their own check. It also explicitly preserves
the limitation that multiple uses of the subset-pair inequality cannot
reuse the same middle-fiber mass without accounting for it.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
